setupWizard.admission.ask.note: You approve each new printer by its code. This is the safe choice.
setupWizard.admission.ask.title: Ask me first
setupWizard.admission.lead: A printer that connects for the first time shows a code on its screen.
setupWizard.admission.open.note: A printer joins as soon as it connects. Choose this only on a network you trust.
setupWizard.admission.open.title: Approve every printer
setupWizard.admission.title: How does a new printer join?
setupWizard.aside.tagline: Your printers, on a server of your own
setupWizard.code.label: Setup code
setupWizard.code.lead: A few questions follow. Your answers stay in this browser until you confirm them at the end, so a reload loses nothing. Passwords and the code stay in this tab only. The server changes nothing until you confirm, except the certificates you ask it to make.
setupWizard.code.missing: Enter the setup code the server shows.
setupWizard.code.title: Let us set up this server
setupWizard.code.where: The server shows this code in the window where it runs, and in its log. In a container, read it with docker logs. When the configuration sets a code, use that one. When the server restarts, it shows a new code.
setupWizard.done.keptEarlier: The server kept its earlier settings, because it could not start with your answers.
setupWizard.done.lead: Your answers are written and the server runs on them.
setupWizard.done.title: This server is ready
setupWizard.done.webOff: The server runs without its web app. Use the API at /api/v1, and read how at /docs.
setupWizard.encryption.downloadBrowser: Download the root certificate for browsers
setupWizard.encryption.generate.note: The server makes its own root certificate and signs the certificates with it. This is the easy choice for a home or a workshop.
setupWizard.encryption.generate.title: Create certificates for me
setupWizard.encryption.guide.address: When printers use an address, write it twice in the certificate, as IP and as DNS.
setupWizard.encryption.guide.ecdsa: A printer takes ECDSA keys only, so make the key with prime256v1 as above.
setupWizard.encryption.guide.files: Enter the paths of server.crt and server.key above, and copy connect.der to the printer's USB stick.
setupWizard.encryption.guide.lead: These commands make a root certificate, a certificate signed by it for one name, and connect.der for printers. They need openssl and bash or zsh, which macOS and Linux have.
setupWizard.encryption.guide.title: How to make your own certificate
setupWizard.encryption.hostInvalid: Enter only a name or an address, without http://, at most 20 characters. A port may follow, as in 192.168.1.24:8481.
setupWizard.encryption.hostLoopback: At this name a printer finds itself, not this server. Enter the address of the server on the network.
setupWizard.encryption.lead: At home you can leave both off. Turn them on when the server is reachable from a network you do not trust.
setupWizard.encryption.listener.hostHint: The name or the address printers reach this server at on the network, never localhost. A printer stores at most 20 characters of it. When a connection is encrypted, it has to be one of the names in the certificate. In a container, enter the host's address. Add the published port when printers reach it through a different port than this page, as in 192.168.1.24:8481. Otherwise, the wizard chooses the port automatically.
setupWizard.encryption.listener.plain: The web app speaks a newer TLS than printers do, so printers connect on a port of their own, without encryption.
setupWizard.encryption.listener.portHint: Write it as :8443. It cannot be the port of the web app.
setupWizard.encryption.madeBefore: The certificates were created earlier. Create them again to download the root certificate.
setupWizard.encryption.missingPair: Enter the certificate file and the key file.
setupWizard.encryption.namesHint: Every name and address browsers and printers use to reach this server, one on each line.
setupWizard.encryption.own.note: Give the paths of a certificate and its key in PEM on the computer that runs the server. A certificate for printers has to use an ECDSA key.
setupWizard.encryption.own.title: Use my own certificate files
setupWizard.encryption.printers.declared: Your configuration file declares how printers connect, so this step changes nothing there.
setupWizard.encryption.printers.hint: Printers connect over TLS, on a port of their own. Each printer needs the root certificate from a USB stick.
setupWizard.encryption.printers.label: Encrypt printer connections
setupWizard.encryption.title: Should the connections be encrypted?
setupWizard.encryption.usb.copy: Copy connect.der to the top folder of a USB stick.
setupWizard.encryption.usb.ini: After the setup, the page that adds a printer gives you prusa_printer_settings.ini. Copy it to the same stick.
setupWizard.encryption.usb.load: On the printer, open Settings, Network, Prusa Connect, and choose Load settings.
setupWizard.encryption.usb.title: What each printer needs
setupWizard.encryption.web.hint: The browser and every program that uses the API connect over HTTPS.
setupWizard.encryption.web.label: Encrypt the web app (HTTPS)
setupWizard.failed.lead: It went back to the settings it had before. Enter the new setup code the server shows, change the answer that caused this, and confirm again.
setupWizard.failed.title: The server did not start with these settings
setupWizard.field.error.choice: Choose one of the values offered.
setupWizard.field.error.duration: Write a duration such as 30s, 5m or 6h.
setupWizard.field.list: Write one value on each line.
setupWizard.field.locked: Set in {file}. That value is used.
setupWizard.field.reference: This key in the configuration reference
setupWizard.hint.adminHandover: An administrator can hand the organisation to somebody else through the API. Off, only this file can do it.
setupWizard.hint.allowedOrigins: Other web pages that may call this server from a browser, such as a dashboard you host yourself. Leave it empty if you only use the web app of this server.
setupWizard.hint.apiAddr: The port the web app uses, written as :8080, and the printers too unless they have a port of their own. Write a host before the colon, such as 192.168.1.10:8080, to listen on one network only.
setupWizard.hint.clientId: The name this server was given when you registered it at the sign-in provider.
setupWizard.hint.connLifetime: How long one database connection is used before a new one replaces it.
setupWizard.hint.dashboards: The home page made of cards you arrange yourself. Off, the home page is the list of printers, or the printer's page when there is only one.
setupWizard.hint.discovery: Announce this server on the local network, and find the printers there that have PrusaLink turned on.
setupWizard.hint.discoveryHidden: Announce nothing on the network, so PrusaSlicer does not find this server. It still hears the printers.
setupWizard.hint.discoveryServices: The names the server announces itself under on the network. Keep the default unless a guide tells you otherwise.
setupWizard.hint.dsn: This is the address of your Postgres database, with the user and the password, such as postgres://user:password@host:5432/database.
setupWizard.hint.engine: Where the server keeps its data. sqlite is a file on this computer and needs nothing else. postgres is a database server you run yourself.
setupWizard.hint.heartbeat: How often an open live update stream sends a small sign of life, so a proxy does not close it.
setupWizard.hint.issuer: Sign in at a provider you already run, such as Keycloak or Authentik, through OpenID Connect. Leave it empty to use no provider.
setupWizard.hint.language: The language the web app uses when a browser asks for none of these.
setupWizard.hint.listingCache: Memory for the folder listings of printers, so a folder opens at once the second time.
setupWizard.hint.localLogin: People sign in with a password stored on this server. It cannot be on together with a sign-in provider.
setupWizard.hint.logFormat: Write text for a log you read in a window, or json for a log collector such as Loki or Elasticsearch.
setupWizard.hint.logLevel: How much the server writes to its log. Use debug when you look for a problem, and info the rest of the time.
setupWizard.hint.marketplace: List the extensions from the Prusa marketplace on the Extensions page.
setupWizard.hint.marketplaceTimeout: How long the Extensions page waits for the marketplace before it shows an error.
setupWizard.hint.marketplaceUrl: Where the list of extensions comes from. Change it only to use a marketplace of your own.
setupWizard.hint.maxIdle: How many of those connections stay open while nothing happens.
setupWizard.hint.maxOpen: How many database connections the server may open at once.
setupWizard.hint.maxStreams: How many live update streams one person may have open, which is about how many tabs. When nobody signs in, everybody shares this limit.
setupWizard.hint.memoryLimit: The most memory the server tries to use, in bytes. Empty means the limit in GOMEMLIMIT, or no limit. Set it on a small computer that runs other things too.
setupWizard.hint.metrics: Serve numbers about the server for Prometheus and Grafana at /metrics. Off, that address answers 404.
setupWizard.hint.metricsAddr: A separate port for the metrics, written as :9090. That port asks for no sign-in, so keep it off the public network.
setupWizard.hint.moduleSettings: The largest settings record one extension may save.
setupWizard.hint.pageCache: Memory for SQLite, for each connection. More makes large lists faster.
setupWizard.hint.passwordHashes: How many sign-ins the server checks at the same time. Lower it on a small computer.
setupWizard.hint.passwordMemory: How much memory checking one password uses. More is safer against password guessing, and slower on a small computer.
setupWizard.hint.passwordPasses: How many times one password check goes over that memory. Less memory needs more passes.
setupWizard.hint.previewCache: Memory for print file previews, so they show at once the second time. Lower it on a small computer.
setupWizard.hint.principal: The user every request runs as when nobody signs in. The first administrator is created under this id, which is not the name they sign in with.
setupWizard.hint.printerAddress: The address printers connect to, when it is not the address you opened this page on. Set it when the server is behind a proxy or has a public name.
setupWizard.hint.printerCustomCa: Turn this on when the printers' certificate is signed by your own root certificate. Each printer then needs connect.der on its USB stick.
setupWizard.hint.redirectUri: The address of this server that the provider sends people back to after they sign in. Register the same address at the provider.
setupWizard.hint.requestTimeout: How long the server works on one request before it gives up. The default suits almost everybody.
setupWizard.hint.retry: How long a browser waits before it reconnects after the live update stream drops.
setupWizard.hint.serverName: This name shows in the browser tab, at the top of the menu and on the local network.
setupWizard.hint.shutdownTimeout: How long the server waits for open requests when it stops, and then for each part of the server to stop.
setupWizard.hint.site: The name of this server in every event it sends. Give each server its own name when you connect several of them.
setupWizard.hint.stateBudget: How much reported state the server keeps for each printer. Keep the default unless the log says a printer reports more.
setupWizard.hint.statementTimeout: How long one database query may run on Postgres before it is stopped.
setupWizard.hint.streamTimeout: How long a live update stream or a file transfer may run. A large print file on a slow printer needs a long limit.
setupWizard.hint.theme: The page is light, dark, or the same as the computer.
setupWizard.hint.thumbnailDisk: Keep thumbnails of files on printers on disk, so a restart does not ask the printers again.
setupWizard.hint.thumbnailDiskBytes: Disk space for thumbnails of files on printers. The oldest are removed when it is full.
setupWizard.hint.thumbnailPrefetch: Ask an idle printer for the thumbnails of its files before anybody opens them.
setupWizard.hint.tlsCertificate: Use HTTPS instead of plain HTTP. Enter the path of a certificate file on this computer. Leave it empty for plain HTTP, which is fine on a home network.
setupWizard.hint.tlsKey: This is the private key of the certificate above. Fill both fields or neither.
setupWizard.hint.trustedProxies: The addresses of a reverse proxy in front of this server, such as nginx or Traefik, one on each line. The server then sees the real address of each visitor.
setupWizard.hint.webApp: Serve this web app. Turn it off only when another program talks to the server through its API.
setupWizard.history.forever: As long as the disk allows
setupWizard.history.hint: The server keeps temperature charts, events, the command log and finished transfers in a file of its own. The list of print jobs is kept either way.
setupWizard.history.label: Keep the history of each printer
setupWizard.history.retentionHint: Older samples and events are removed. The command log and the transfers are kept. A longer time needs more disk space.
setupWizard.identity.custom.note: Using a sign-in system other than OpenID Connect, such as LDAP or SAML? An extension connects it to this server.
setupWizard.identity.lead: Choose whether people sign in. You can add more people later in the settings.
setupWizard.identity.missingUsername: Enter the name the administrator signs in with.
setupWizard.identity.oidc.note: People sign in at a provider you already run, such as Keycloak, Authentik or Google. This server keeps no passwords.
setupWizard.identity.oidc.title: Sign in with your own provider
setupWizard.identity.open.note: Anyone who can reach this server can use it. Choose this only for a computer nobody else can reach.
setupWizard.identity.open.title: Nobody signs in
setupWizard.identity.passwordLong: Use at most 72 bytes. A letter with an accent takes two.
setupWizard.identity.passwordsDiffer: The two passwords are not the same.
setupWizard.identity.required.note: You create the first administrator now. Choose this when other people can reach this server.
setupWizard.identity.required.title: Everybody signs in
setupWizard.identity.title: Who may use this server?
setupWizard.key.stateBudget: State kept per device, in bytes
setupWizard.key.title: Server name
setupWizard.language.label: Language
setupWizard.mqtt.hint: Send the state of every printer to an MQTT broker you run.
setupWizard.mqtt.label: MQTT
setupWizard.mqtt.namespace: The server sends the state under topics that start with v1/. The documentation lists every topic.
setupWizard.mqtt.urlHint: Write tcp://host:1883, or ssl://host:8883 when the broker uses TLS.
setupWizard.mqtt.urlInvalid: Write an address such as tcp://broker.local:1883.
setupWizard.oidc.badSubject: A subject has at most 255 characters and no spaces.
setupWizard.oidc.clientIdHint: The ID this server is registered under at the provider.
setupWizard.oidc.clientSecretHint: Fill it in when the provider gave you one: Google, and most providers' web clients. Leave it empty for a public client.
setupWizard.oidc.issuerHint: The provider's address. The server reads /.well-known/openid-configuration from it.
setupWizard.oidc.notUrl: Enter a full address starting with https:// or http://.
setupWizard.oidc.redirectUriHint: Register this address at the provider. Leave it empty to use the one shown.
setupWizard.oidc.step.client.failed: The provider refuses the client ID or secret.
setupWizard.oidc.step.client.passed: The provider accepts the client ID and secret.
setupWizard.oidc.step.client.skipped: Not tried, because the provider's address does not work.
setupWizard.oidc.step.client.unknown: The provider's answer about the client could not be read.
setupWizard.oidc.step.discovery.failed: The provider's address does not work.
setupWizard.oidc.step.discovery.passed: The provider answers and offers what a sign-in needs.
setupWizard.oidc.step.discovery.unknown: The provider's answer could not be read.
setupWizard.oidc.step.redirect.failed: The provider refuses the redirect address or the client ID.
setupWizard.oidc.step.redirect.passed: The provider takes the redirect address.
setupWizard.oidc.step.redirect.skipped: Not tried, because the provider's address does not work.
setupWizard.oidc.step.redirect.unknown: The provider's answer about the redirect address could not be read.
setupWizard.oidc.subject: Administrator's subject (sub)
setupWizard.oidc.subjectHint: The administrator's ID at the provider, its sub claim. Whoever signs in with it administers this server.
setupWizard.oidc.tryHint: Signs nobody in. Nothing is saved.
setupWizard.path.advanced.note: You set almost every setting of the server, one part at a time: the network, the database, the log, security and limits.
setupWizard.path.advanced.title: Advanced
setupWizard.path.basic.note: Only the choices most people make. Every other setting keeps a default that works.
setupWizard.path.basic.title: Basic
setupWizard.path.lead: Both paths end on a summary of your answers. Nothing changes until you confirm, except the certificates you ask the server to make.
setupWizard.path.title: How much do you want to set up now?
setupWizard.section.access.lead: How much work checking one password takes. More is safer against guessing, and slower on a small computer.
setupWizard.section.access.title: Passwords
setupWizard.section.database.lead: The database that keeps the printers, the jobs and the people.
setupWizard.section.database.title: Where is the data stored?
setupWizard.section.logging.lead: How much the server writes to its log, and the metrics it serves.
setupWizard.section.logging.title: What should the server report?
setupWizard.section.look.lead: The name, the language and the colours of the web app, and where extensions come from.
setupWizard.section.look.title: How should it look?
setupWizard.section.network.lead: The address the browser and the printers use, and how the server shows itself on the local network.
setupWizard.section.network.title: How is this server reached?
setupWizard.section.server.lead: The name of this server, its memory limits and how it stops.
setupWizard.section.server.title: Anything else?
setupWizard.steps.label: Setup steps
setupWizard.storage.declared: Your configuration file already names a folder for uploads, so the server keeps it.
setupWizard.storage.label: Folder
setupWizard.storage.lead: The files you upload for printing are kept in a folder on the computer that runs the server.
setupWizard.storage.nas: A folder on a NAS works too. Connect the share on this computer first, then give its path here.
setupWizard.storage.noParent: No part of this path exists
setupWizard.storage.notAFolder: This path is a file, not a folder.
setupWizard.storage.notWritable: The server cannot write to this folder.
setupWizard.storage.pickAnother: Choose another folder, or give the user that runs the server the right to write here.
setupWizard.storage.providers: Other places to keep files, such as Amazon S3, Google Drive and Nextcloud, are coming.
setupWizard.storage.ready: The folder is ready, and the server can write to it.
setupWizard.storage.title: Where should files be kept?
setupWizard.storage.willCreate: The server creates this folder when you confirm.
setupWizard.summary.fileWins: The wizard cannot change a setting that {file} sets. These settings keep the value from that file:
setupWizard.summary.fileWinsEncryption: A certificate and its key only work together, so the wizard cannot finish. Go back to the encryption step and use the values from the file, or change the file.
setupWizard.summary.fileWinsIdentity: The sign-in provider settings only work together, so the wizard cannot finish. Go back to the sign-in step and use the values from the file, or change the file.
setupWizard.summary.lead: Check your answers. Confirm writes them to {file} and restarts the server.
setupWizard.summary.moves: After the restart the server answers at {address}.
setupWizard.summary.others: Every other setting stays as it is now.
setupWizard.summary.title: Ready?
setupWizard.summary.unchanged: Every setting stays as it is now.
setupWizard.summary.webOff: The web app is off, so the server then answers only its API at /api/v1 and the reference at /docs.
setupWizard.summary.webOffTitle: Without a web page from here on
setupWizard.theme.label: Theme
setupWizard.timeout.lead: Read the window or the log where the server runs. It says what went wrong. To try again, use the new setup code it shows.
setupWizard.timeout.title: The server did not come back
setupWizard.wait.lead: This takes a few seconds. Keep this page open.
setupWizard.wait.moved: The server now answers at {address}. This page opens it in a moment.
setupWizard.wait.title: Restarting the server
setupWizard.welcome.lead: This server connects your printers and gives you one place to watch them, send them files and control them. It runs on a computer of your own, and no cloud account is needed.
setupWizard.welcome.pointLater: You can change most answers later.
setupWizard.welcome.pointLocal: Your printers and files stay on your network.
setupWizard.welcome.title: Welcome to Prusa Connect
